mainTopic: רב איקא's wine-related wages, the משנה on יין נסך falling on food (נותן טעם לפגם), and רבא's ruling on wheat soaked with יין נסך
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about רב איקא. He poured kosher wine into non-Jews' wineskins and was paid with the empty jugs. אביי permits this because his work was done while the wine was still permitted. The גמרא raises two challenges, and each time shows that he had no stake in the forbidden wine and did no work with it. A new משנה follows. יין נסך on whole grapes can be rinsed off, but cracked grapes become forbidden. Figs and dates are forbidden only if the wine's flavor improves them, so ביתוס בן זונן's figs were permitted because the flavor spoiled them (נותן טעם לפגם). Finally, רבא rules on wheat that יין נסך fell on. After a challenge from a כלאים garment, he allows it only as bread sold to גוים with no Jew present, and רב פפא explains that wheat's slits make it like cracked grapes.

steps.title: רב איקא pours wine for non-Jews and is paid in jugs
steps.stepSummary: The story: רב איקא poured wine into non-Jews' wineskins, ferried them across the river, and took the empty jugs as his pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He used to pour wine for non-Jews, then ferry them across the river, and they paid him with the jugs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a case story that sets up a question about whether this way of earning money is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once wine is in a non-Jew's possession it becomes forbidden, and a Jew may not profit from it. Here רב איקא's payment, the jugs, is linked to the wine deal, so the story raises a worry.

phrases.english: He would pour wine for gentiles,
phrases.notes: "He" is רב איקא, named just before this line.

phrases.english: and go ferry them across the river crossing,
and they would give him the jugs as payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: pouring, ferrying, and payment in jugs.

steps.title: אביי permits it because the work was done with permitted wine
steps.stepSummary: People report רב איקא to אביי, who says his work happened while the wine was still kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: People came and told אביי. He answered: when he was working, he was working with permitted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his ruling: רב איקא did nothing wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is timing. When רב איקא poured, the wine was still kosher. It only became forbidden afterward, once it was in the non-Jews' hands. So his labor, and the pay he got for it, came from permitted wine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the guiding principle for the rest of the section: payment is fine if the work was done while the wine was permitted.

phrases.english: They came and told Abaye;
he said to them: when he was laboring,
he was laboring with permitted wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case described in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב איקא allowed to take jugs as pay in this wine deal?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. His work was done while the wine was still permitted.

steps.title: Challenge: he still cares that the wine stays safe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב איקא wants the wineskins not to burst, so he still has a stake in the forbidden wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he wants the wine preserved, so that the wineskins don't tear!
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after pouring, רב איקא benefits if the wine stays safe. If a wineskin burst, the buyers might take back the jugs he got as pay. So he seems to have an interest in the wine after it already became forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: wants it to last / stay intact

phrases.english: But he wants it to stay intact,
phrases.notes: If the wineskins burst, he could lose the jugs he was paid with.

phrases.english: that the wineskins should not tear!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רב איקא only dealt with permitted wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He still has an interest in the wine after it became forbidden, since his pay depends on it staying safe.

steps.title: Answer: he made a deal, or they brought spare barrels
steps.stepSummary: Two answers: he agreed in advance that a burst wineskin was the buyers' loss, or the buyers brought barrels as backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's where he made a condition with them. Or else, where they brought barrels with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: a deal says his pay is safe no matter what happens, so he has no stake in the wine. Answer two: the buyers have barrels ready if a wineskin tears, so nothing he cares about is at risk. Either way, he doesn't care whether the forbidden wine survives.

phrases.english: Where he made a condition with them.
phrases.notes: The deal was that if a wineskin burst, it was their loss, and he kept the jugs.

phrases.english: Alternatively, where they brought barrels with them.
phrases.notes: The two bracketed words are two spellings of the same word for barrels; the square-bracket one is the corrected wording.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: He depends on the wine surviving.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of a prior deal or backup barrels, he has no stake in the wine.

steps.title: Challenge: ferrying them is work with forbidden wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ferrying the buyers and their wine across the river happens after the wine is already forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he ferries them across the crossing, which is working with forbidden wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge to אביי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer covered the pouring, which happened while the wine was still permitted. But the ferrying comes later, when the wine is already forbidden. So part of his paid work seems to involve forbidden wine.

phrases.english: But he ferries them across the crossing,
which is laboring with forbidden wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on אביי's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that all his work was with permitted wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ferrying takes place after the wine became forbidden.

steps.title: Answer: the ferryman did the work, not him
steps.stepSummary: Two answers: he arranged with the ferryman in advance, or he had signal knots agreed with the ferryman. Either way, he did not do the ferrying himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's where he told the ferryman from the start. Or else, where they held knots with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge in two ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב איקא never carried the forbidden wine himself. In the first answer, he arranged with the ferryman beforehand to take these people across. In the second, he used agreed signal knots so the ferryman would know to take them. Since the ferryman did the work, רב איקא did not labor with forbidden wine.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי allows רב איקא's pay because every bit of his own work was done with permitted wine. He also had no stake in the wine once it was forbidden, and others did the later work.

phrases.english: Where he told the ferryman from the start,
Alternatively, where they held knots with him.
phrases.notes: Knots were an agreed signal with the ferryman to take these people across.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 and closes the story.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He himself ferried the forbidden wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ferryman did it, by prior arrangement or signal knots.

steps.title: משנה: libation wine on grapes
steps.stepSummary: If יין נסך falls on grapes, you rinse them and they are permitted. If the grapes were cracked, they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If libation wine fell on grapes, one rinses them and they are permitted. If they were cracked, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the rule for יין נסך that spills onto grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whole grapes have a closed skin, so the wine stays on the outside and rinsing removes it. Cracked grapes let the wine soak inside, where rinsing can't reach, so they become forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ יֵין נֶסֶךְ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָבִים —
phrases.english: MISHNA: Libation wine that fell on grapes —
one rinses them and they are permitted,
but if they were cracked — they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ יֵין נֶסֶךְ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, unrelated to the story before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whole grapes: rinse and permitted. Cracked grapes: forbidden.

steps.title: משנה: libation wine on figs or dates
steps.stepSummary: If the wine falls on figs or dates, they are forbidden if the wine adds flavor to them (נותן טעם).
steps.simpleTranslation: If it fell on figs or dates, and there is enough wine to give them flavor, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a different rule for figs and dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs and dates soak up liquid, so rinsing is not enough. The test becomes נותן טעם: if the wine is strong enough to flavor the fruit, the fruit is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: gives flavor (the test for whether a mixture is forbidden)

phrases.english: If it fell on figs
or on dates,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: if there is enough in them to give flavor — it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Figs and dates are forbidden if the wine gives them flavor.

steps.title: The story of ביתוס בן זונן's dried figs
steps.stepSummary: A barrel of יין נסך broke onto ביתוס בן זונן's dried figs on a ship, and the חכמים permitted the figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once ביתוס בן זונן brought dried figs on a ship. A barrel of libation wine broke and spilled on them. He asked the חכמים, and they permitted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a true story where the חכמים ruled the figs permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is a real case of libation wine falling on figs. Yet the ruling was lenient, so the wine here must not have counted as forbidding the figs.
steps.confusionAlert: This story can look like it clashes with step 8, where wine on figs can forbid them. The משנה's general rule in step 10 and the גמרא in steps 11–12 explain the difference: here the wine spoiled the figs' taste.
steps.whatToRemember: Grapes: rinse, unless cracked. Figs and dates: forbidden if the wine adds flavor. In ביתוס's case, the חכמים permitted the figs.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Baytos ben Zunen
who brought dried figs on a ship,
and a barrel of libation wine broke
and fell on them,
and he asked the Sages and they permitted them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case about figs, connected to the rule in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ביתוס's case, the dried figs were permitted.

steps.title: The general rule: improving flavor forbids, non-improving flavor permits
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up its rule. If the food is improved by the forbidden flavor, it is forbidden. If it is not improved, it is permitted, like vinegar falling on split beans.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the principle: anything that is improved by the flavor it absorbs is forbidden. Anything that is not improved by the flavor it absorbs is permitted, like vinegar that fell onto split beans.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its discussion with one clear rule that covers all the earlier cases about wine falling on food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is not only whether the forbidden item gave flavor, but whether that flavor helped the food. Vinegar does not make split beans taste better, so the beans stay permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the principle: a summary rule that covers many cases
Benefit. Here it means the food is improved by the flavor

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the source for the well-known idea of נותן טעם לפגם: forbidden flavor that spoils the food does not make it forbidden.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
Anything that benefits from the flavor it absorbs is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בַּהֲנָאָתוֹ בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: anything that does not benefit from the flavor it absorbs is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן חוֹמֶץ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי גְּרִיסִין.
phrases.english: such as vinegar that fell onto split beans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the earlier rulings of the משנה about wine falling on grapes, figs and dates, and the story of ביתוס בן זונן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden flavor makes food forbidden only if it improves the food. If it does not improve the food, the food is permitted.

steps.title: Why does the story seem to contradict the ruling right before it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה brings a story that seems to go against the ruling just before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Is an incident brought to contradict the ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the order of the משנה. The משנה said figs that get the wine's flavor are forbidden, then told a story where figs were permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a story in a משנה is brought to support the ruling. Here the ruling said figs are forbidden if they take on flavor (step 8), but the story says the חכמים permitted ביתוס's figs (step 9). That looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story, often brought as a real-life ruling

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is an incident brought to contradict the ruling?
phrases.notes: This is about the ביתוס story, which comes right after the rule that figs with the wine's flavor are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's ruling and story (steps 8 and 9) and asks how they fit together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the משנה: a ruling forbidding figs, followed by a story permitting figs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should support the ruling before it, but this story seems to give the opposite result.

steps.title: A line is missing: flavor that spoils the food is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing a line. It should say that flavor that spoils the food is permitted, and the ביתוס story is an example of that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: if the flavor spoils the food, the food is permitted. And there was also an incident with ביתוס בן זונן, who was bringing dried figs on a ship. A barrel of יין נסך broke and fell on them. The case came before the חכמים, and they permitted the figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by adding a missing line to the משנה, so the story now supports the ruling instead of contradicting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs are forbidden only when the wine makes them taste better. When wine spoils the taste of dried figs, the figs are permitted. ביתוס's case was that kind of case, so the story fits.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing something: a common way the גמרא fills in words
And this is what it is teaching
Gives flavor that spoils the food

steps.whatToRemember: Forbidden flavor that spoils the food (נותן טעם לפגם) does not make it forbidden. The ביתוס בן זונן story is the example.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the משנה is wrong. חסורי מיחסרא means a line is understood but not written, and the גמרא is spelling it out.

phrases.english: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִפְגָם הוּא — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: if the wine gives flavor that spoils the food, it is permitted,
and there was also an incident with ביתוס בן זונן
who was bringing dried figs on a ship,
and a barrel of יין נסך broke
and fell on them,
and the case came before the חכמים, and they permitted them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by filling in a missing line of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to permit figs even though the ruling forbade figs that take on flavor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling forbids figs only when the flavor improves them. The story was a case of spoiling flavor, which is permitted.

steps.title: רבא allows wheat soaked with יין נסך to be sold to גוים
steps.stepSummary: Wine of יין נסך fell on a heap of wheat. רבא allowed it to be sold to גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a heap of wheat on which a barrel of יין נסך fell. רבא permitted it to be sold to גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where רבא ruled on wheat that soaked up יין נסך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא did not let a Jew eat the wheat, but he allowed selling it to גוים. That means he allowed a Jew to get benefit (money) from it.

phrases.english: There was a certain heap of wheat
phrases.notes: Some versions say כרי, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is כַּרְיָא. Both mean a heap.

phrases.english: on which a barrel of יין נסך fell,
רבא permitted selling it to גוים.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא כַּרְיָא דְּחִיטֵּי דִּנְפַל עֲלֵיהּ חָבִיתָא דְּיֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's cases to a new practical case of wine falling on food, this time about selling it to גוים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wheat that absorbed יין נסך may be sold to גוים.

steps.title: Challenge from a garment with lost כלאים, which may not be sold to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר ליואי challenges רבא from a ברייתא: a garment with lost כלאים threads may not be sold to a גוי or made into a donkey's saddlecloth, but it may be used as shrouds for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר ליואי challenged רבא: a garment in which כלאים got lost may not be sold to a גוי, and may not be made into a saddlecloth for a donkey. But it may be made into shrouds for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר ליואי brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רבא's ruling about selling to גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a forbidden garment may not be sold to a גוי even though a גוי may wear כלאים. The usual worry is that a Jew might later buy it from the גוי without knowing. If so, the same worry should stop רבא from letting the wheat be sold to גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mix of wool and linen in clothing (שעטנז)
A saddlecloth placed on an animal
A dead person with no one else to bury him

steps.confusionAlert: The garment is not forbidden to the גוי himself. The question is only whether a Jew may hand it over, since it could come back to a Jew.

phrases.english: רבה בר ליואי raised an objection to רבא:
A garment in which כלאים got lost,
phrases.notes: Linen threads got mixed into a wool garment and can't be found, so the whole garment is treated as forbidden.

phrases.english: one may not sell it to a גוי,
and may not make it into a saddlecloth for a donkey,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ תַּכְרִיכִין לְמֵת מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: but one may make it into shrouds for a מת מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in step 13 using a ברייתא about a forbidden garment.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission to sell the wheat soaked with יין נסך to גוים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids selling a forbidden garment to a גוי, which suggests forbidden items may not be sold to גוים, since they might come back to a Jew. So the wheat should not be sold either.

steps.title: The reason behind the garment rule also applies to the wheat
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר ליואי explains why the כלאים garment may not be sold to a גוי: the גוי might resell it to a Jew. The same danger exists with רבא's wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why may the garment not be sold to a גוי? Because he might sell it to a Jew. Here too, the גוי might sell the wheat to a Jew!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר ליואי finishes his challenge to רבא. He spells out the reason behind the ברייתא and applies it to the wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids selling the garment to a גוי out of worry that it will end up with a Jew who does not know it is forbidden. Wheat soaked in יין נסך carries exactly the same risk. So רבא's permission to sell the wheat to גוים seems to clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same applies here

phrases.english: To a gentile, what is the reason it may not be sold?
Perhaps he will come to sell it to a Jew.
Here too, he will come to sell it to a Jew!
phrases.notes: "Here" means רבא's case of the wheat that the wine fell on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 14 by stating the reason behind the ברייתא and applying it to רבא's case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the wheat may be sold to גוים (step 13).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא bans selling a forbidden item to a גוי because he may resell it to a Jew. That same worry applies to the wheat, so selling it should also be forbidden.

steps.title: רבא changes his ruling: grind, bake, and sell away from Jews
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes back his first ruling. He now allows the wheat to be ground and baked into bread, then sold to גוים when no Jew is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא changed his mind. He allowed them to grind the wheat, bake it into bread, and sell it to גוים, as long as no Jew was there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the challenge and gives a new ruling. The wheat is still sold to גוים, but only after it becomes bread and only with no Jew around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the item would reach a Jew. Selling it as bread, and only where no Jew is present, makes it unlikely that a Jew will end up buying it. So the challenge is handled by changing how the sale is done, not by banning the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in front of a Jew

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a ruling can be adjusted to remove a specific worry, without dropping the basic permission.

phrases.english: He went back and permitted
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, changing the ruling he gave in step 13.

phrases.english: grinding them and baking them
and selling them to gentiles,
not in the presence of a Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge of step 15 by revising רבא's original ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wheat soaked with יין נסך may be ground, baked, and sold to גוים, but not in the presence of a Jew.

steps.title: The משנה says uncracked grapes only need rinsing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: grapes that יין נסך fell on are permitted after rinsing, unless they are cracked. So uncracked produce should be fine after rinsing. Why not just rinse the wheat?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if יין נסך fell on grapes, you rinse them and they are permitted. If they were cracked, they are forbidden. This means only cracked grapes are forbidden, and uncracked ones are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole discussion about the wheat from a משנה about grapes. If rinsing works for whole grapes, it should work for wheat too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids only cracked grapes, because the wine soaks inside them. Whole grapes just need a rinse. The challenge is that wheat should be treated like whole grapes, so all of רבא's steps would be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes … no (used to draw an inference)

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna: libation wine
that fell on grapes,
one rinses them and they are permitted.
But if they were cracked, they are forbidden.
Cracked ones, yes, they are forbidden;
ones that are not cracked, no, they are not forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: יֵין נֶסֶךְ שֶׁנָּפַל עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge: why does the wheat need any special treatment at all?
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in רבא's case that the wheat is forbidden and cannot simply be rinsed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From the משנה, uncracked produce is permitted after rinsing. Wheat should be like uncracked grapes, so rinsing should be enough.

steps.title: Wheat counts like cracked grapes because of its slits
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that wheat is different. Each kernel has a slit, so wine gets inside, just as with cracked grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: wheat is different. Because of its slits, it is like cracked grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from the משנה. Wheat cannot be compared to whole grapes, because its built-in slits let the wine soak in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing works only when the wine stays on the outside. A wheat kernel has a natural crease, so the wine gets absorbed, just like with a cracked grape. That is why the wheat is forbidden and רבא's ruling was needed.
steps.whatToRemember: Wheat soaked with יין נסך is treated like cracked grapes, because its slits absorb the wine. So it cannot just be rinsed, and רבא allowed it only as bread sold to גוים away from Jews.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Wheat is different,
since, because of its slits,
phrases.notes: He means the natural crease that runs along every wheat kernel.

phrases.english: it is similar to cracked grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by showing that wheat belongs with cracked grapes, not whole ones.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: wheat has a different physical nature than whole grapes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wheat is like whole grapes, so rinsing should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wheat's slits make it like cracked grapes, so the wine soaks in and rinsing does not help.
